title: Product PRD & Release: Unified Inference — Overview, Requirements, Roadmap, Pricing and Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document bundles the product overview, PRD, design specifications, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging notes, and the initial release notes for the Unified Inference product line (vNext). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and go-to-market stakeholders.

1) Product overview

Overview:
- Product name: Unified Inference (UIF) — vNext
- Goal: Provide a single, opinionated inference runtime and control plane that delivers predictable latency, cost efficiency, and consistent developer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Primary users: ML engineers, platform teams, product teams integrating LLM features.

Key capabilities (high level):
- Single API surface for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Model routing (latency/cost region-aware) with automatic fallbacks
- Built-in caching and batching suggestions (Redwood Optimize integrations)
- Dedicated and private deployment parity (same config and rollout behavior)
- Observability and cost attribution per-token and per-route

Success metrics (90-day targets after GA):
- Adoption: 35 enterprise customers migrating at least one production route to UIF
- Performance: 99th percentile tail latency <= 120ms for standard text-generation workload (50-token requests) on hosted tier
- Cost efficiency: 20% average per-token cost reduction relative to baseline serving configuration via Optimize recommendations
- Reliability: SLO uptime 99.95% for hosted API endpoints

Owners & stake:
- Product lead: Aisha Patel
- Eng director (runtime): Marcus Lee
- Eng PM (deployments): Priya Kaur
- Sales lead: Nora Gupta

2) PRD and requirements

Problem statement:
Teams face fragmented inference runtimes across deployment modes, inconsistent SLAs, and unpredictable cost/latency tradeoffs. This slows adoption and increases TCO. UIF must unify serving semantics and provide meaningful knobs for cost/latency tradeoffs while remaining simple to operate.

High-level product requirements (MUST):
- RQ-001: Unified API parity — same REST/SDK surface for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (endpoints, params, error models).
- RQ-002: Model routing policies — support at least: latency-first, cost-first, region-preference, and customer-tier overrides.
- RQ-003: Fallbacks — automatic fallback to compatible model variants (quantized or smaller family) when primary is unavailable, with configurable thresholds.
- RQ-004: Observability — per-request token cost, model attribution, KV-cache hit rates, and 99/95/50 latency histograms exposed to Console and metrics pipeline.
- RQ-005: Optimize integration — run-time suggestions for batching, caching, and quantization profile per route.
- RQ-006: Security & compliance — TLS-by-default, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs for model loads/rollouts.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- NFR-001: 95th percentile latency degradation <= 10% when routing through private deployments vs hosted baseline.
- NFR-002: Support autoscaling policies for Dedicated with min/max capacity and burst buffer.
- NFR-003: API backwards compatibility for top-10 customer routes for at least 18 months.

Constraints (known):
- C-001: Some third-party open models have incompatible kernels that require per-model kernel selection (added integration cost).
- C-002: Private on-prem installs must support air-gapped upgrade paths and offline license validation.

Requirements table (summary):
| ID | Title | Priority | Acceptance criteria | Owner |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| RQ-001 | Unified API parity | Must | Identical endpoint names and params documented; SDKs pass feature parity tests | Eng SDKs |
| RQ-002 | Model routing policies | Must | 4 policy types implemented; policy simulator for validation | Eng runtime |
| RQ-003 | Fallbacks | Must | Can automatically redirect to fallback model within 120ms; rollback path verified | Eng runtime |
| RQ-004 | Observability | Must | Console and metrics contain per-route token cost and latency histograms | Eng platform |
| RQ-005 | Optimize integration | Must | Optimize suggestions are surfaced in Console with projected savings | Product/Optimize PM |

3) Design specifications (implementation notes)

Architecture overview:
- Control plane: Centralized policy engine (Redwood Control) that stores route configs, model pins, and rollout policies. Exposes gRPC API for runtime agents.
- Runtime agents: Lightweight agents in hosting plane (hosted/dedicated/private) that perform model selection, batching, and caching.
- Cache layer: KV prefix cache co-located on GPU nodes with configurable TTL and memory quotas.
- Metrics pipeline: Kafka -> Prometheus exporter -> Timeseries DB (M3) and Console dashboards.

Key design choices and rationale:
- Continuous batching vs fixed micro-batches: use continuous batching with latency-aware cutoffs to reduce tail latency while improving throughput for low QPS routes. Rationale: better cost-performance for mixed workloads.
- Model fallback semantics: implement optimistic routing — primary attempt to preferred model with soft timeout (configurable, default 80ms) then non-blocking fallback attempt, returning fastest successful model. Rationale: minimize latency impact while preserving quality.
- KV cache placement: per-GPU process cache to avoid cross-host traffic and leverage local memory. Eviction policy: LFU with TTL.

API surface (high level):
- POST /v1/generate — params: model, max_tokens, temperature, route_policy, pin_model_version, stream
- POST /v1/chat — params: messages[], tools[], function_call_policy, stream
- GET /v1/route-configs/{route_id} — returns route-specific SLO and model pin

Data contracts and schema examples (JSON string in docs):
- Example route config JSON displayed in Console (kept as text here for UI):
  {
    "route_id": "orders-rewrite-prod",
    "policy": "latency-first",
    "primary_model": "redwood-llama-70b",
    "fallbacks": ["redwood-llama-13b-8q", "redwood-llama-7b-4q"],
    "soft_timeout_ms": 80,
    "pin_model_version": "2028-03-01"
  }

Performance targets (engineering acceptance):
- Unit throughput: support 8k concurrent steady-state requests per GPU shard for 32-token average responses (with continuous batching).
- Cold start: model load < 90s for 70B warmed on common instance types for Dedicated setups; provide pre-warm tooling.

Security considerations:
- All control-plane communications require mTLS and short-lived certificates.
- Private deployments must expose only configured management ports to customer VPCs.
- Audit events: model load/unload, route config changes, KMS accesses — retained for 1 year by default.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)

Themes by quarter (milestones):
- Q2 2028 (Discovery & Alpha): policy engine prototype; basic routing simulator; SDK parity tests; alpha of Optimize suggestions in Console.
- Q3 2028 (Beta): runtime agents v1 with KV cache, fallback flow; Dedicated autoscaling controls; initial Private deployment reference architecture.
- Q4 2028 (GA): production-ready hosted offering, SLA 99.95%, pricing and packaging live, enterprise onboarding playbooks.
- Q1 2029 (Expansion): feature parity for private air-gapped upgrades, additional model family support, expanded observability retention options (12+ months).

Roadmap dependencies and risks:
- Dependency on kernel optimizer library (third-party) for some model families — risk: performance regressions during upgrades. Mitigation: integration tests and staged kernel rollouts.
- Dependence on cloud GPU availability for Dedicated expansion — mitigation: multi-cloud partnerships and burst capacity designs.

Milestones and owners (high level):
- Policy engine GA (Owner: Eng Platform) — target: 2028-07-15
- Runtime agents Beta (Owner: Eng Runtime) — target: 2028-09-01
- Console Optimize suggestions v1 (Owner: Product/Optimize) — target: 2028-08-01

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing principles:
- Usage-based first: per-token generation and per-vector embedding units remain the core billing signals.
- Value add-ons: Dedicated reserved capacity contracts, longer observability retention, SLAs and compliance packages.
- Cost transparency: surface per-route projected savings from Optimize suggestions and cost impact for routing policies.

Suggested packaging tiers (draft):
- Hosted Standard (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token; Console with 30d retention; community support.
- Hosted Enterprise: committed usage discount tiers, 99.95% SLA, 90d retention, SSO and role-based access, priority support.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly/annual), autoscaling controls, 365d audit logs (add-on), custom SLAs.
- Private: license + deployment fee, enterprise support, air-gapped option, professional services for onboarding.

Illustrative pricing (draft for GTM):
- Generation: $0.0035 / 1k input tokens + $0.012 / 1k output tokens (hosted standard).
- Embeddings: $0.0008 / vector (hosted standard).
- Dedicated: starting at $8k/month per reserved GPU shard (varies by region and GPU type).
- Private: one-time deployment + annual subscription — quoted per-customer.

Add-ons and commercial levers:
- Extended observability retention: $X per GB-month
- Model pinning SLA add-on (guaranteed pinned-version availability): premium pricing
- Professional Services: onboarding, quality tuning, custom evals — fixed-fee engagements

6) Release notes (initial public release: GA 2028-10-10)

Release: Unified Inference v1.0 (GA) — 2028-10-10
Highlights:
- Unified API parity across Hosted and Dedicated
- Model routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-preference, customer-tier)
- Automatic fallback flow with soft timeout semantics
- Console integration for Optimize suggestions and per-route cost visibility
- Dedicated autoscaling controls and burst capacity

Breaking changes and migration notes:
- Clients using experimental route_config field must migrate to new /v1/route-configs API. Migration script available in SDK v1.8.
- Backwards compatibility: standard generation/chat endpoints remain unchanged; test suite and migration docs included.

Known issues (GA):
- Some 3rd-party kernels show transient performance regressions on new driver versions — workaround: pinned kernel version in Dedicated until patch release.
- Private air-gapped installer v1 lacks automatic telemetry uploader (manual bundle required).

Rollout and launch plan (high level):
1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks): migrate 5 internal customer routes, monitor SLOs and cost delta. Owner: Eng SRE
2. Early access (4 weeks): invite 10 pilot customers (mix of startups and enterprise) with dedicated onboarding and PS hours. Owner: Customer Success
3. Gradual GA (4 weeks): staged ramp to public hosted offering, enable Dedicated reservations. Owner: GTM & Sales Ops

Operational playbook (incident readiness):
- SLO targets: 99.95% uptime for hosted routes, error budget 0.05% per monthly window.
- On-call runbook references: see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/unified-inference-oncall (link)
- Escalation path: tier1 -> Eng Runtime -> Eng Platform -> Product
